subject: Term sheet: staged prepay drawdown & ramp schedule options
body:
From: Maya Singh <maya@horizonhealth.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-07-01 09:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Exploring multi-year commitment options

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team liked the latency and the cost profile you showed. We are now trying to map financials so procurement and finance can evaluate a multi-year commitment vs. an annual prepay. High level: expected usage profile looks like ~200M tokens Y1, ~300M tokens Y2 with a fairly steep ramp in Q2 of Y2 as we roll out an additional feature.

Two specific asks from procurement:
- Can you give us a clear prepay drawdown model (wallet) that supports monthly burn reporting and a defined ramp schedule? We need to show spend over time for our forecasting.
- What term discounts are available for a 2-year commitment if we prepay upfront vs. an annual prepay with true-up? Any proposed mechanics for unused prepay at the end of year 1 (roll-over vs. sweep)?

I've attached a short procurement requirements doc.

Maya
Procurement
Horizon Health

Attachment: Horizon-Prepay-Requirements.pdf (1 page)

-------------------------------------------
From: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
To: Maya Singh <maya@horizonhealth.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-07-01 11:02 -0700
Subject: Re: Exploring multi-year commitment options

Maya — thanks, and appreciate the clarity on the ramp. Below is a concise set of options tailored to the usage numbers you provided. I’m copying Marcus (sales lead) and Laura (finance) for the accounting/contract nuances.

Option A — Annual prepay wallet (single year)
- Upfront prepay for Year 1 usage estimate; monthly burn reported to Horizon.
- Discount: 10% off list for full Year-1 prepay.
- True-up at year end for overage/underuse; underuse can be rolled up to a 6-month carry-forward if agreed in advance.
- Invoicing: one upfront invoice + monthly reporting.

Option B — 2-year staged prepay (recommended for lower unit cost)
- Total 2-year commitment with staged prepay drawdown (flexible wallet model).
- Suggested payment schedule: 60% upfront at contract signing (applies to Year 1+Y2 credit), 20% at start of Y2, 20% at mid-Y2.
- Delivered discount: 18% on blended unit price for the two-year committed volume.
- Wallet mechanics: single logical wallet that draws monthly; monthly statements show draw, remaining balance, and projected runway at current burn.
- Ramp handling: we can set scheduled top-ups (automatic or manual) tied to agreed ramp milestones so you never hit surprise throttles.
- End-of-period treatment: unused prepay at contract end can be either refunded at a nominal rate (to avoid revenue recognition issues) or converted to a short-term support credit — we can include language either way in the SOW.

Notes/assumptions:
- Discounts and payment schedule are negotiable if you need a different revenue recognition profile.
- Our platform supports monthly token-level reporting and exportable CSVs for your forecasting systems.
- For security/compliance questions we can provide SOC2 artifacts and region-specific hosting notes (cc Marcus).

Next step: I’ll share a draft quote + SOW for Option B and we can iterate on payment cadence and contract language. If you want, we can also propose an escrowed wallet flow that only releases funds to usage buckets on a monthly basis (helpful for finance teams that want tighter controls).

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jasmine_liu@redwood.ai

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai, Maya Singh <maya@horizonhealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-07-02 09:14 -0700
Subject: Re: Exploring multi-year commitment options

Quick operational notes from finance/sales leadership:

- Discount floor and accounting: Laura, can you confirm if a 60/20/20 collection schedule is workable from a revenue recognition perspective? We typically prefer some upfront to de-risk capacity. If Horizon needs evenness for budgeting, we can structure 50/25/25 but that will shift the blended discount ~150–200bps.
- Wallet sweep behavior: two models we offer — (1) Roll-forward: unused tokens roll for up to 6 months, (2) Sweep/Refund: unused prepaid converted at 50% cash-back to the customer at term end. We generally recommend Roll-forward for early-stage rollouts, Sweep for larger guarantees.
- Suggested contract clause for ramp: include a scheduled top-up trigger tied to a mutually agreed metric (e.g., feature launch date or MQA of active users). This avoids ad-hoc negotiation during ramp.

Laura — can you prepare a short note on the accounting implication (ASC/IFRS) for both models (roll-forward vs sweep) and the preferred invoice language? I’ll include that in the legal/commerce checklist.

-Marcus
VP Sales | Redwood Inference

From: Raghu Patel <raghu@horizonhealth.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Cc: Maya Singh <maya@horizonhealth.com>
Date: 2026-07-03 14:55 -0700
Subject: Re: Exploring multi-year commitment options

Thanks Jasmine/Marcus — this is helpful. A few procurement items before we move to legal:

1) Can you confirm the wallet drawdown report format? Our finance system needs a CSV with date, token_count_consumed, SKU, remaining_balance.
2) Data residency & audit logs: we need confirmation that logs for production traffic are retained for 13 months and that hosting is in US region.
3) Invoicing cadence: will Horizon receive a single invoice per prepay payment? Can we get Net-45 terms on the non-upfront payments?
4) Contract: please share a redline-ready SOW and the commercial quote. We will push this to legal after procurement signs off.

Attaching our procurement agenda.

Raghu Patel
Sr. Manager, Procurement
Horizon Health

From: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
To: Raghu Patel <raghu@horizonhealth.com>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya@horizonhealth.com>, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-07-07 08:21 -0700
Subject: RE: Exploring multi-year commitment options — Proposed term sheet

Raghu / Maya — appreciate the quick turnaround. Attached is a one-page term sheet plus the draft SOW and quote reflecting Option B (2-year staged prepay with 60/20/20 schedule and 18% blended discount). Key points in the term sheet:

- Wallet reporting: CSV export daily with fields: date_utc, sku, tokens_consumed, tokens_remaining, wallet_id. We will provide a sample CSV with the quote.
- Logs & residency: production logs retained for 13 months; primary hosting region: us-west-2. We will include SOC2 certification and the data processing addendum in the contract.
- Invoice cadence: we will issue one invoice per scheduled payment. Net-45 is acceptable for payments after the initial upfront invoice.
- End-of-term treatment: default will be 6-month roll-forward for unused prepaid tokens. If Horizon prefers a partial refund, we can add a 50% refund clause instead.

Next steps:
1) Review attached term sheet, quote, and SOW.
2) If acceptable, I’ll generate a legal redline packet + DocuSign link.
3) Request: sign by 2026-07-20 to lock the 18% blended rate and the proposed ramp schedule.

I’ll be on a short customer site visit July 8–9 but reachable by email. Happy to hop on a call the week of July 13 to finalize.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
